summary: Interrogated the PH-2 plan against forge_cli/roadmap.py and the live plans/roadmap.json. One claim in the plan was simply wrong, and one acceptance criterion was unreachable with the commands the plan proposed. Both were fixed in the plan before this grill was recorded. The scope boundary — save_roadmap and the status routes stay unvalidated — held under pressure.
gaps: The plan named roadmap import as the only route that writes epics. cmd_derive also accepts an epics list and validates it with check_epics; it is simply the pre-sign-off route, gated on generated_by: docs-decomposer. The real shape of the problem is that BOTH epic-writing routes are closed after sign-off, not that only one exists.

Acceptance criterion 8 requires this repo's stories to point at an epic, and no route can do that. cmd_assign writes an assignee and cmd_link_spec writes a spec; nothing writes a story's epic field. As planned, PH-2.4 would have had to hand-edit plans/roadmap.json — the exact move the evidence rules forbid — or silently fail.

The plan did not say what tightening check_epics does to its existing callers. Requiring objective and source_refs changes a function derive and import already call, so the blast radius needed stating rather than discovering during implementation.
contradictions: The plan promised the backfill would run 'through the new command rather than by hand' while specifying only epic add, which creates an epic and cannot attach a story to it. The plan asserted a capability it did not provide.
resolutions: Problem section corrected: both derive and import write epics, both are closed after sign-off, and this repo's roadmap has no epics key at all and no story carrying an epic field.

Added forge roadmap set-epic as acceptance criterion 4 and folded it into PH-2.2 alongside epic add, with the reason stated: an epic nothing can point a story at leaves the backfill exactly as blocked as it is now. Task ordering now requires PH-2.4 to follow PH-2.2.

Added a risk naming the check_epics widening: all three routes author epics so the requirement lands where epics are written, a stored roadmap with bare epics is never revalidated because save_roadmap stays unvalidated by design, and a test re-saves a legacy roadmap whose epics predate the contract.
Scope, Surface Impact, Task Decomposition and the test list were all realigned onto two new routes rather than one.
open_items: non-blocking: the derived-ordering decision this plan records is written but unaccepted until a human confirms it in chat. PH-3 consumes that decision to justify removing build_waves; if it has not landed when PH-3 records its decomposition, PH-3 restates the ordering claim in its own Technical Approach rather than assuming it.

non-blocking: this worktree's base predates main's acceptance of decisions 0017 and 0018, so decisions_reviewed lists fifteen rather than seventeen. The plan attests what its base carries; rebasing onto a main that has PH-1's sign-off pin is the fix, and it is a merge-ordering question rather than a plan defect.

non-blocking: epic add requires sign-off but not the epics-approved decision, unlike import. Deliberate — import replaces the whole list, add appends one — but it is a genuine asymmetry a reader will notice.
